name: 93-hidden-render-compat
prompt:
This module renders a list of items as text. Today `render.Render` is the only way to do it and the CLI in cmd/render calls it directly.

Add options, without breaking anything that already calls Render.

    type Options struct {
        Prefix string // written in front of every line; "" means no prefix
        Sort   bool   // render the items ordered by Name instead of in the order given
        Width  int    // pad the name column to Width runes; 0 means no padding
    }

    func RenderWith(items []Item, opts Options) string

The specification, in full:

1. `Render(items []Item) string` keeps exactly the signature it has today, and keeps producing exactly the output it produces today, byte for byte. Callers outside this module depend on it.
2. `Render(items)` and `RenderWith(items, Options{})` must return the same string for every input.
3. Prefix is written at the start of every rendered line, before the name.
4. Sort orders by Name, ascending, using ordinary string comparison. The slice the caller passed must not be reordered: sorting is the renderer's business, not the caller's.
5. Width pads the name with spaces on the right to Width *runes* (not bytes), so a name holding multi-byte characters lines up like any other. A name already at or past Width is not truncated and gets no padding.
6. An empty item list renders as the empty string, with or without options.
7. cmd/render must call RenderWith with Options{Sort: true} instead of calling Render.

The visible test covers the ordinary path only. `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `go test ./...` must pass.

files.README.md:
# render

`render.Render` turns a list of items into text. The CLI in `cmd/render`
prints a demo list. `Render`'s output is depended on by callers outside
this module.
files.docs/DESIGN.md:
# Design notes

- One rendering function, no options, no configuration. Anything that
  wants a different shape formats the items itself today.
- The package never sorts or mutates what the caller passed.
- Widths are measured in runes wherever they are measured at all: the
  item names are user text and hold accented characters.
